You would leave the catheter open to free drainage rather than use a valve when you need accurate hourly urine output, as with critically ill or post-operative patients. You would also avoid a valve when the bladder has high pressure, poor compliance, or a risk of reflux into the kidneys, and when the patient cannot reliably sense bladder fullness or operate the valve. This assumes you mean a urinary catheter drainage valve, as in my earlier answer.

CONFIDENCE: 70
